title: Inventory Audit and Fee Standard for the Kestrel Dealer Wholesale Floorplan Line
content:
**Standard.** Fees can be billed only while the line status is active, credit hold or wind-down. Audits are made every audit frequency period of the grade and billed the grade's audit fee; a unit not found must be produced within the grade's missing-unit cure period in business days or it is treated as sold out of trust. Each unit sold out of trust is billed the sold-out-of-trust fee and must be paid off immediately; when the units sold out of trust on an audit reach the grade's credit hold threshold the line is placed on credit hold. Interest unpaid after its due date is billed the late interest fee percent of the unpaid interest, never less than the late interest fee minimum.

Kestrel audits floored inventory on the Kestrel Dealer Wholesale Floorplan Line unannounced. Each completed audit records its date, the units counted and verified, and the units found sold out of trust; that audit date becomes the line's latest audit date. The periods, fees and threshold are those of the line's Kestrel Wholesale Risk Grade.

## Fees and the line status

The status gate is read from the system record of the line the fee is billed on, as it stands before billing.

| Line status | Fees can be billed |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Credit hold | Yes |
| Wind-down | Yes |
| Pending documentation | No |
| Closed | No |

Three kinds of fee are billed: the audit fee, the sold-out-of-trust fee (recorded against the unit's VIN) and the late interest fee. Each fee billed is added to the line's interest due balance, the balance of billed but unpaid interest and fees.

## Units not found and units sold out of trust

- A unit not found at audit must be produced within the grade's missing-unit cure period, counted in business days; a unit not produced within it is treated as sold out of trust.
- Each unit sold out of trust is billed the sold-out-of-trust fee and must be paid off immediately.

## Credit hold

On an active line, a credit hold stops new advances; it follows a sold-out-of-trust finding or a payment default, and records the audit that triggered it. Under this standard the hold is placed when the count of units sold out of trust on one audit reaches the grade's credit hold threshold. Hypothetical threshold of 2: an audit finding 1 unit sold out of trust is below it; an audit finding 2 or more reaches it.

## Late interest fee (hypothetical figures)

The late interest fee is the higher of the late interest fee percent of the interest left unpaid after its due date and the late interest fee minimum. With a hypothetical percent of 4 and a hypothetical minimum of 40 USD, invented for illustration:

| Unpaid interest after the due date | Percent of the unpaid interest | Fee billed |
|---|---|---|
| 600 USD | 24 USD | 40 USD, the minimum |
| 1000 USD | 40 USD | 40 USD |
| 2500 USD | 100 USD | 100 USD |
